This planned prompt-level sensitivity analysis replaces the three duration
variables with their corresponding frequency variables. Duration and frequency
never enter the same model. Frequency is coded 0--3 after the verified 1--4 to
0--3 recode. All temporal, covariance, mediation, Bayesian iteration, and
reporting decisions otherwise match the primary prompt-level DSEM.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE,
  collapse = FALSE, comment = NA, dev = "svglite"
)
required_packages <- c(
  "bruceR", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "knitr", "MplusAutomation",
  "openxlsx", "readxl", "rmarkdown", "svglite", "tibble", "tidyr"
)
available <- vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(available)) {
  stop("Missing required R packages: ", paste(names(available)[!available], collapse = ", "))
}
locate_step4_helper <- function(start) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(candidate)) candidate <- dirname(candidate)
  repeat {
    helper <- file.path(candidate, "Step_4_Dynamic_Structural_Equation_Modeling",
                        "S4_0_DSEMHelpers.R")
    if (dir.exists(file.path(candidate, "Step_1_Descriptive_and_Reliability")) &&
        file.exists(helper)) return(helper)
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) break
    candidate <- parent
  }
  stop("Could not locate S4_0_DSEMHelpers.R in the public project")
}
input_context <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)

helper_file <- locate_step4_helper(project_start)
source(helper_file, local = TRUE, encoding = "UTF-8")

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)
input_file <- file.path(project_root, "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis", "dat_step4_dsem.rda")
primary_file <- file.path(
  project_root, "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis", "fit_s4_2_primary_prompt_dsem.rda"
)
result_file <- file.path(
  project_root, "Res_2_Data_for_Analysis", "fit_s4_4_frequency_sensitivity_dsem.rda"
)
table_file <- file.path(

)
figure_file <- file.path(
```

# Load and validate prompt-level frequency data

```{r load-data}
dat_step4_dsem <- load_single_object(input_file, "dat_step4_dsem")
primary_fit <- load_single_object(primary_file, "fit_s4_2_primary_prompt_dsem")
prompt <- dat_step4_dsem$prompt |>
  dplyr::arrange(Name_ID, tprompt) |>
  as.data.frame()
model_data <- prompt |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id = as.integer(factor(Name_ID, levels = sort(unique(Name_ID)))),
    tprompt = as.integer(tprompt),
    dayc = as.numeric(dayc), tm2 = as.numeric(tm2), tm3 = as.numeric(tm3),
    fi = as.numeric(InteractiveFrequency),
    fa = as.numeric(ActiveFrequency),
    fp = as.numeric(PassiveFrequency),
    core = as.numeric(Core), peri = as.numeric(Peripheral), dist = as.numeric(Distress)
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()

frequency_values <- unlist(model_data[c("fi", "fa", "fp")], use.names = FALSE)
frequency_values <- frequency_values[!is.na(frequency_values)]
stopifnot(
  nrow(model_data) == 18810L,
  dplyr::n_distinct(model_data$id) == 209L,
  !anyNA(model_data[c("id", "tprompt", "dayc", "tm2", "tm3")]),
  !anyDuplicated(model_data[c("id", "tprompt")]),
  all(tapply(model_data$tprompt, model_data$id, function(x) identical(x, 1:90))),
  all(frequency_values %in% 0:3),
  identical(sort(unique(frequency_values)), as.numeric(0:3))
)
input_audit <- data.frame(
  rows = nrow(model_data), clusters = dplyr::n_distinct(model_data$id),
  scheduled_prompts_per_cluster = min(table(model_data$id)),
  observed_interactive_frequency = sum(!is.na(model_data$fi)),
  observed_active_frequency = sum(!is.na(model_data$fa)),
  observed_passive_frequency = sum(!is.na(model_data$fp)),
  minimum_frequency = min(frequency_values), maximum_frequency = max(frequency_values),
  fully_missing_six_outcomes = sum(
    rowSums(!is.na(model_data[c("fi", "fa", "fp", "core", "peri", "dist")])) == 0L
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(input_audit)
```

# Mplus model specification with frequency replacement

```{r model-specification}
variable_block <- paste(
  "CLUSTER = id;",
  "WITHIN = dayc tm2 tm3;",
  "LAGGED = fi(2) fa(2) fp(2) core(1) peri(1) dist(1);",
  "TINTERVAL = tprompt(1);",
  sep = "\n"
)
model_block <- six_variable_model_block(
  engagement = c("fi", "fa", "fp"), controls = c("dayc", "tm2", "tm3")
)
assert_free_engagement_lag_paths(
  model_block, engagement = c("fi", "fa", "fp")
)
constraint_block <- six_variable_constraint_block()
focal_dictionary <- six_variable_focal_dictionary(
  engagement = c("fi", "fa", "fp"),
  predictor_names = c(
    "InteractiveFrequency", "ActiveFrequency", "PassiveFrequency"
  )
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(focal_dictionary) == 27L,
  !anyDuplicated(focal_dictionary$key),
  all(nchar(focal_dictionary$key) <= 8L),
  !grepl("li|la|lp", variable_block),
  grepl("LAGGED = fi(2)", variable_block, fixed = TRUE)
)
knitr::kable(focal_dictionary)
```

# Fixed 80,000-iteration two-chain canonical run

The estimates were generated on 2026-09-14 with Mplus 9.0
(output header: `Mplus VERSION 9`), using the original seed, two chains and
80,000 fixed iterations. The header retains the historical report date.

```{r run-80k}
run_80k <- run_bayes_dsem(
  data = model_data,
  variable_block = variable_block,
  model_block = model_block,
  constraint_block = constraint_block,
  usevariables = names(model_data),
  mplus_directory = mplus_directory,
  stem = "s4_4_frequency_sensitivity_dsem",
  title = "! Six-variable prompt-level frequency-replacement sensitivity DSEM.",
  iterations = 80000L, seed = 69427L, expected_clusters = 209L,
  mplus_command = mplus_command,
  expected_mplus_version = expected_mplus_version,
  parameter_scale = "stdyx"
)
stopifnot(run_80k$convergence$passed)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  run = "80k", final_psr = run_80k$convergence$final_psr,
  max_second_half_psr = run_80k$convergence$max_second_half_psr,
  passed = run_80k$convergence$passed
))
```

# H3: Engagement to Peripheral versus Core

The three within-person contrasts compare the lag-1 Engagement-to-Peripheral
path with the corresponding Engagement-to-Core path: `h3i = aip - aic`,
`h3a = aap - aac`, and `h3p = app - apc`. These are signed differences of the
existing free coefficients. Adding these derived parameters does not constrain
or otherwise change the model body. Positive values indicate a stronger
positive association with subsequent Peripheral symptoms. A 95% HPD interval
entirely above zero supports the hypothesized direction; an interval entirely
below zero supports the opposite direction; an interval including zero leaves
the directional comparison uncertain.

The contrasts use **unstandardized** coefficients for the two symptom means
on their common 1--5 response scale. They are not differences of STDYX
coefficients. This sensitivity test uses frequency (0--3) in place of duration and one scheduled prompt as the lag unit; it evaluates the corresponding frequency contrast.
All 13 defined parameters (six indirect effects, three indirect contrasts,
`bdiff`, and the three H3 contrasts) are exported in the separate
`MODEL_CONSTRAINT_Raw_80k` sheet. The 14 focal STDYX paths remain in their own sheet.

```{r h3-contrasts}
h3_contrasts_80k <- model_constraint_raw_80k |>
  dplyr::filter(key %in% c("h3i", "h3a", "h3p")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    directional_conclusion = dplyr::case_when(
      lower_hpd > 0 ~ "Peripheral > Core: supported",
      upper_hpd < 0 ~ "Core > Peripheral: opposite direction",
      TRUE ~ "95% HPD includes zero: uncertain"
    )
  )
stopifnot(identical(h3_contrasts_80k$key, c("h3i", "h3a", "h3p")))
knitr::kable(
  h3_contrasts_80k |>
    dplyr::select(mode, estimate, posterior_sd, lower_hpd, upper_hpd,
                  directional_conclusion),
  digits = 5,
  col.names = c("Engagement mode", "Posterior median", "Posterior SD",
                "95% HPD lower", "95% HPD upper", "Directional conclusion"),
  caption = "H3 lag-1 contrasts: Peripheral minus Core (unstandardized)."
)
```

# Interpretation of STDYX path coefficients

The following statements use Mplus STDYX coefficients. Each coefficient is the
estimated standard-deviation change in the outcome associated with a one-standard-
deviation increase in the predictor, conditional on the remaining lagged
variables and the Day/Time nuisance controls.

```{r generated-interpretations, results='asis'}
interpret_rows <- focal_stdyx_80k |>
  dplyr::filter(role %in% c(
    "Engagement to mediator", "Mediator to Distress",
    "Lag-1 Engagement to Distress adjustment", "Lag-2 direct effect"
  ))
make_frequency_interpretation <- function(row) {
  predictor_label <- if (is.na(row$mode)) row$predictor else paste0(row$mode, " frequency")
  direction <- if (row$estimate >= 0) "higher" else "lower"
  uncertainty <- if (row$lower_hpd <= 0 && row$upper_hpd >= 0) {
    " The 95% HPD interval included zero."
  } else {
    " The 95% HPD interval excluded zero."
  }
  temporal <- switch(
    row$role,
    "Engagement to mediator" = paste0("subsequent ", row$outcome),
    "Mediator to Distress" = "subsequent Distress",
    "Lag-1 Engagement to Distress adjustment" = "subsequent Distress",
    "Lag-2 direct effect" = "Distress two scheduled prompts later"
  )
  paste0(
    "- When a participant's ", predictor_label,
    " was one standard deviation higher, ", temporal,
    " was estimated to be ", sprintf("%.3f", abs(row$estimate)),
    " standard deviations ", direction,
    " (STDYX posterior median; 95% HPD [", sprintf("%.3f", row$lower_hpd), ", ",
    sprintf("%.3f", row$upper_hpd), "]).", uncertainty, "\n"
  )
}
cat(paste(vapply(seq_len(nrow(interpret_rows)), function(i) {
  make_frequency_interpretation(interpret_rows[i, , drop = FALSE])
}, character(1)), collapse = ""))
```

# Figure and reproducible exports

```{r export-results}
plot_data <- focal_stdyx_80k |>
  dplyr::filter(role %in% c(
    "Engagement to mediator", "Mediator to Distress",

  )) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    display = dplyr::case_when(
      role == "Engagement to mediator" ~ paste(mode, "to", outcome),
      role == "Lag-2 direct effect" ~ paste(mode, "direct to Distress"),
      role == "Mediator to Distress" ~ paste(predictor, "to Distress"),
      role == "Lag-1 Engagement to Distress adjustment" ~ paste(mode, "lag-1 to Distress"),
      TRUE ~ paste(mode, "lag-2 to Distress")

    display = factor(display, levels = rev(unique(display)))

  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.5) +
```

This sensitivity changes the Engagement measurement metric, not the temporal
ordering. Comparisons with the duration model therefore emphasize posterior
direction and 95% HPD zero-exclusion patterns rather than raw coefficient
magnitudes.
